signal: EliseAI raised a $250M Series E at a $2.2B valuation in August 2025 and plans to triple headcount, including sales and SDR hiring.

email.body1:
Matthew, saw EliseAI closed its $250M Series E and is set to triple the team, sales and SDRs included.

Tripling headcount means new reps ramping while the in-market list keeps growing, and follow-up volume is usually the first thing that slips. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so your team books meetings instead of chasing: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to your top three target accounts. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through them?
email.body2:
Matthew, quick follow-up for EliseAI.

When a team scales this fast, every new rep brings a slightly different version of the playbook, and response rates drift before anyone notices. A tight, consistent motion is the fastest lift while you ramp.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Matthew, last bit of proof for EliseAI.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

Want to grab time so I can walk you through how your reply rate compares to other fast-scaling startups? I pulled a quick benchmark.
email.body4:
Matthew, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If taking follow-up volume off your reps isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Ramping a tripled team is its own full-time job right after a raise.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your SDR team? I'll tailor it to EliseAI either way.
